title: Credit friction and activation notebook
content:
Notes to self — sketching a small set of starter bundles and how much credit friction to apply for activation. Rough, heuristic first pass.

Context / goal:
- We want a low-friction onramp that (a) gets devs to a meaningful first success, (b) doesn’t gift too much free token/time that destroys conversion economics, (c) surfaces product hooks (streaming, function calls, embeddings) so they build usage patterns.
- Focus: hosted API; assume most signups are small teams or individual devs.

Assumptions and baseline unit costs (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline infra cost (amortized): we use a mix of A100-like GPUs in Dedicated; ballpark = $3.5 / GPU-hour effective marginal cost after infra+ops. (very rough)
- Inference throughput (generation): small-model quantized path: ~10k tokens/s per GPU for batched decode; large models slower. For mixed workloads, assume 3k tokens/s per GPU as conservative.
- Effective tokens per GPU-hour = 3,000 tokens/s * 3600 s = 10.8M tokens/hour.
- Token cost (infra) = $3.5 / 10.8M ≈ $0.000000324 per token ≈ $0.000324 per thousand tokens (k-token).
- Round up to include overhead (scheduling, storage, KVs): multiply by 1.6 → ~$0.00052 / 1k tokens. Call it $0.0005 / 1k tokens infra cost.
- Add support/infra margin + biz overhead → want gross margin target at 70%; price needed ≈ infra_cost / 0.3 ≈ $0.0017 / 1k tokens. So public payg price near $0.0015–$0.002 / 1k tokens plausible for small models. (This is just a sanity check vs market.)

Embeddings special-case:
- Embedding CPU path / batched GPU: more efficient. Assume 30–50M embeddings tokens/hour equivalent; cost per embedding call ~ $0.0000001–0.0000002. We simplify: treat embeddings as cheap relative, price with minimum floor.

Starter credit sizing — heuristics:
- Activation goal = user performs 3 meaningful calls: 1 embed, 1 generate short prompt (200 tokens), 1 chat session (~800 tokens). Target free credit that covers ~2–3 days of light exploration.
- Simple plan: give $20 credit (monetary equivalent). How many tokens is that at our price? If price $0.0017 / 1k tokens → $20 buys ~11.8M tokens. At infra cost that’s ~22x cost (okay). But $20 may be too generous and create churn.

Small credit tiers to test (experiments):
- A: Lightweight trial — $5 credit (goal: immediate API call, basic experiments)
  - At $0.0017 / 1k → 2.9M tokens (~3M). Could cover ~3 small prototypes.
- B: Developer starter — $12 credit
  - ~7M tokens. Good for embedding index + several chats.
- C: Product trial — $30 credit
  - ~17.6M tokens. Enables real stress testing of feature in staging.

Hypotheses on friction and activation sequencing:
1) Soft gating: credit applied on sign-up, but API keys throttle to low qps (e.g., 5 rps) for first 24h to reduce fraud and cost spikes.
2) Feature gating: encourage embedding usage by giving an embedding bonus (extra tokens only usable for embedding endpoints) — drives product value and retention.
3) Conversion friction: require billing method collection only at second milestone (e.g., after $X of usage or after 14 days) to reduce drop-off.

Back-of-envelope conversion math (very approximate):
- New signups/day: 2,000 (current run-rate of marketing channel sampled)
- Activation rate (meaningful API use within 7 days): baseline 18%
- Convert-to-billed within 60 days (after trial): 3% of signups (needs improvement)
- LTV of converted customer (avg) = $3,000 over 12 months (placeholder)
- CAC per signup (marketing only) = $40 (current channel) — quite high; this is for later cohort.

If we move to $12 standard starter credit:
- Spend per user = $12 of free credit costs company (but actual infra cost maybe $0.5–$2 per trial depending usage pattern). Need to compute marginal cost: not full $12.
- Suppose average trial usage consumes 20% of credit in the free period = $2.4 consumed, infra cost = $2.4 * (infra_cost / price) ~ $2.4 * (0.3) ≈ $0.72. So company bears <$1 infra cost per trial on average.
- If conversion rate rises from 3% → 6% due to better credit sizing and product hooks, CAC_effective = CAC / conv ~ $40 / (0.06) ≈ $667 LTV/CAC dynamics change positively.

Activation patterns and product hooks (operational notes):
- Embedding-first flow: prompt user to "build an index from a sample doc" in onboarding. Embedding API calls are cheap and encourage later generation calls (higher margin).
- Sessionization: credit bucket resets/decays over 30 days, but we allow extension via credit-earning actions (invite teammate, share sample app) — reduces cash-free-gift risk, encourages viral loops.
- Reserve a small fraction of credit for function-call testing (simulate function outputs) to ensure developers test tool calling end-to-end.

Risk modes and fraud mitigation:
- Heavy initial usage (bots) can burn expensive generation tokens: throttle per-key by default, extra manual review for high-extract consumers in first 24–72h.
- Device/IP heuristics + billing method requirement for >X usage. For example: require card on file if predicted 7-day spend > $50 equivalent.

Experiment matrix (priority):
- Exp 1: $5 vs $12 trial credit A/B test — measure activation (7d), conversion (60d), avg tokens consumed in trial, fraud rate.
- Exp 2: Embedding-bonus variant (extra 1k embed calls) vs equal-dollar generic credit — check downstream generation conversion.
- Exp 3: Progressive unlock vs one-time credit: give $4 on signup + $8 after completing onboarding tasks — measure onboarding completeness and conversion uplift.

Metric defs to track for experiments (implement in analytics pipeline):
- signup_id, credit_tier, tokens_consumed_by_type (embed/gen), qps_peak, days_active_in_30, conversion_60d, card_on_file_bool, refund_rate, support_contacts

Quick heuristics for pricing per-route (notes):
- chat-short (<=512 tokens): price higher per-1k (lower latency SLO) — premium $/1k
- long-gen (>2k): can be discounted per token via batching incentives
- embeddings: inexpensive per-call but charge per-embed-unit (floor) to avoid spam

Open TODO / questions:
- Get more accurate infra cost numbers from infra-finance (ask @Ethan for per-model marginal $/hr for top-10 models)
- How do discounts for Dedicated customers change starter-credit calculus? Do not give large credits to accounts that later sign Dedicated without commitment.
- Decide default card-collection policy for >$X trial usage. Where is fraud threshold? (ask SRE/Trust)
- Need a small script to compute exact token equivalence for given price slabs. I should build a small notebook.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Run Exp 1 A/B with n=10k signups per arm or 2 weeks whichever earlier. Collect tokens-by-type and conversion signals.
- Draft onboarding flow copy that nudges embedding-first for new signups. Work with DX (Priya) on microcopy.
- Meet with infra-finance to tighten infra-cost per-model numbers (Ethan).

Random scribbles (ideas):
- "activation stake": give a tiny (time-locked) credit that matures after 7 days to encourage return visits.
- gamify onboarding: small leaderboard for "first embedding index created" — maybe overkill but could help virality for dev community.

End of notebook. Save a copy in the A/B experiments folder once we turn this into a formal plan.
